summary: Anyone staying in Korea for more than 90 days (D-2 and D-4 included) must register and get a residence card (외국인등록증, formerly ARC) within 90 days of entry. You apply at the immigration office that covers your address, after booking a visit on HiKorea. The fee has been KRW 35,000 since 1 Jan 2025 (it was KRW 30,000). The card arrives in about 1–6 weeks, depending on the office.
steps: Book a visit on HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr); applications without a reservation are not accepted at most offices
Go to the immigration office for your address (or the one your university assigns) with the documents
Give fingerprints and a photo, then pay the fee
Collect the card in person or by mail when you are told it is ready
Do not leave Korea while the application is pending unless the immigration office confirms you can
documents: Proof of residence (dorm confirmation, lease contract, etc.)
Tuberculosis test certificate for nationals of designated countries (the list is set by MOJ; universities cite 19–21 countries)
Fee KRW 35,000 (some offices and universities say cash only)
timing: Within 90 days of entry. Processing takes about 1–2 weeks (KHU) to about 6–8 weeks (Mason Korea, Incheon office).

notes: The deadline, the fee and the reservation requirement are verified from official or university pages. Processing time and the TB country list vary; show them as ranges and link the official list. The fee was changed in 2025, so do not hard-code KRW 30,000 (several third-party guides and older university pages still show it). Jurisdiction can differ from where you live: KU GSIS says its students must now use the Sejongno office regardless of address.

summary: Some universities collect residence card applications and submit them to immigration for their students, then hand out the cards on campus. This is decided by each university and is not a right. Hangyul should show it only when the university has confirmed it.
steps: Check whether your university runs a group application for your intake
If it does, give the international office the documents and the fee by its deadline
Pick up the card from the office when you are told it is ready
documents: As for an individual application (form, passport and copy, photo, D-2 visa document, TB certificate if applicable, proof of residence for off-campus students)
timing: Set by the university, but still within 90 days of entry. Mason Korea says the process may take about 6–8 weeks.

sources.title: George Mason University Korea – Alien Registration & Rules
sources.quote: The university will handle the collection and submission of student applications to the Incheon Immigration Office. … students will be notified to pick up their ARCs from Office G404.

notes: Only one university example has been verified. Keep this as a per-university flag (supports_group_arc) that university staff set; never assume it.

summary: After registering, you must report to immigration within 14 days any change of address, change of passport details, or a lost card. Late reports can lead to fines. An address change can also be reported at a community centre or ward office.
steps: Moving (for example from a temporary room to the dorm): report the new address within 14 days
New passport: report within 14 days
Lost card: apply for a new one within 14 days
documents: Proof of new residence (dorm payment receipt / confirmation of residence, or lease contract and the landlord's ID copy)

sources.title: Korea University GSIS – Spring 2026 New Student Orientation (PDF)
sources.quote: You must report certain changes to the Immigration Office promptly within 14 days of occurrence … Change of address can be reported to an Immigration Office / City Hall / Local Gu Office … If you do NOT report changes within 14 days, you will be fined.

notes: The source is a university guide that repeats the MOJ rule. Cross-check against the Immigration Act (law.go.kr) before showing penalty amounts.

summary: The Ministry of Justice has issued a mobile residence card since 10 January 2025. Cards issued from 2025 carry an IC chip for this. Eligibility and setup steps were not verified here.

sources.title: Korea Immigration Service – Get to Know the Newly Launched Mobile Residence Card
sources.quote: The Ministry of Justice began issuing the Mobile Residence Card on January 10, 2025

notes: Mention it only as information until the eligibility and setup steps are checked against the MOJ leaflet.

summary: D-2 students (and D-4-3 school students) are enrolled in NHIS as regional members from the date of entry, or from the date of alien registration if that is later. In practice cover starts at registration, and the first bill arrives about 1–2 months later. Other D-4 trainees, such as language-course students, are enrolled only after 6 months in Korea. Enrollment is automatic and there is nothing to apply for.
steps: Register for your residence card (this triggers enrollment for D-2)
Wait for the insurance card, enrollment notice and bill, which are mailed to your registered address
Set up payment (bank or card auto-debit, or pay the bill)
Keep your address up to date so bills reach you
timing: D-2: from entry, or from alien registration if later. D-4 (general training, except D-4-3): after 6 months in Korea.

sources.quote: D-2 … automatically enrolled in the National Health Insurance on the day of entry; D-4 (General Training): 6 months after your date of entry

sources.title: Korea University GSIS – Spring 2026 New Student Orientation (PDF)
sources.quote: For those who enter the country for the first time, the date of alien registration is the enrollment date for NHI.

notes: Universities word this differently ('day of entry' vs 'date of alien registration'). The NHIS rule reconciles them: entry date, or the registration date if later. Hangyul should say 'cover starts once your residence card application is registered' and link NHIS.

topic: National Health Insurance – premium for students
summary: D-2 and D-4 members get a 50% reduction (since March 2023) on the foreigner regional premium. That premium is at least the national average premium of the previous November. One university notice gives the 2026 student premium as KRW 79,320 a month. It is due by the 25th of each month, paid in advance for the next month. Unpaid premiums can restrict visa extension and other stay permits.
steps: Pay monthly by the 25th (auto-debit is recommended)
Check for unpaid premiums before applying for a visa extension
cost: About KRW 79,320/month in 2026 (university notice; set yearly)

summary: NHIS may not cover you straight after you arrive, because cover starts at registration. Universities strongly recommend arriving with private travel or student insurance that covers Korea. Some language institutes include insurance for D-4 students.
steps: Buy private insurance that covers Korea from your arrival date until NHIS starts
Keep the policy document in English or Korean
timing: From arrival until NHIS starts (usually about 1 month or more)

sources.title: Korea University GSIS – Spring 2026 New Student Orientation (PDF)
sources.quote: it is highly recommended to enter the country with private insurance, which sets Korea as a cover range since there is a possibility that NHI will not take effect upon your arrival

notes: This is a recommendation, not a legal requirement for D-2 students who are covered by NHIS. Do not recommend a specific insurer unless a signed partner agreement exists.

summary: You usually open an account at a branch in person. After you get your residence card, bring the card, your passport and a document showing why you need the account (students: certificate of enrollment). Before the residence card you need your passport plus proof of a Korean address (for example a utility bill, hotel voucher, or dorm or lease confirmation, at the branch's discretion). If purpose documents are missing, the bank opens a restricted account with daily limits of KRW 3M at a branch and KRW 1M at ATMs or online. The limits can be lifted later. Hana Bank lets you pre-register your details before arrival, but the account is still opened at a branch after you arrive.
steps: Choose a bank; many campuses have an on-campus branch
Bring your ID and purpose documents to the branch
Expect a restricted account if you open it before your residence card or without purpose documents
Ask the bank to lift the limits once you have your residence card and enrollment proof
documents: Certificate of enrollment (proof of purpose for students)
Proof of Korean address if you have no residence card yet
Some banks ask for a Korean phone number or a tax ID number
timing: Ideally after the residence card is issued. A restricted account is possible before that.

sources.quote: If some documents are omitted, a restricted bank account … shall be opened … Daily transaction limit: Bank branches KRW 3 million, ATMs KRW 1 million, E-finance KRW 1 million … Documents required if a foreigner needs to open an account before issuance of the residence card: passport … certificate of Korean residency is additionally required

sources.title: Konkuk University student guidebook – Banking services
sources.quote: your passport, Certificate of Enrollment, and Tax Identification Number … Shinhan Bank (Konkuk Branch) located on the 1st floor of the Student Union Building

sources.quote: Upon arrival, the preregistered information will be accessible at all Hana Bank branches nationwide

notes: Requirements differ by bank and branch (InvestKorea says so explicitly). Do not promise remote account opening before arrival. Pre-registration only speeds up the branch visit. The limit figures come from the 2024 KOTRA guide; recheck them each year.

summary: SK Telecom, KT and LG U+ run roaming centres in the Incheon T1 arrivals hall, some open 24 hours near Arrival Hall F. You can get prepaid SIMs or eSIMs with a passport, and carriers sell foreigner eSIM products online too. A regular postpaid contract usually needs the residence card and a Korean payment method, so most students start prepaid and switch after registration.
steps: Before you fly: decide between buying an eSIM online and picking up at an airport counter
On arrival: go to a carrier roaming centre in the arrivals hall (T1: near Arrival Hall A, 06:00–22:00; near Hall F, 24h)
After you get your residence card and bank account: think about a postpaid or MVNO plan
documents: Residence card and Korean bank account or card (postpaid – to be confirmed with the carrier)
timing: On arrival (prepaid); after the residence card (postpaid)

sources.title: Incheon Airport – Facilities: roaming centres (T1)
sources.quote: KT Roaming Center (24H) 00:00 ~ 24:00 Near Arrival Hall F … LG U+ Roaming Center (24H) … SK Telecom Roaming Center (24H) 00:00 ~ 24:00 Near Arrival Hall F on the West Side of 1st Floor, Terminal 1

sources.title: SK Telecom roaming – eSIM (search-result excerpt; page redirect loop on fetch)
sources.quote: LTE eSIM (Data, Call, SMS) products are only for foreigners … intended for short-term travelers to Korea (within 90 days)

notes: Counter locations and hours are verified on airport.kr for T1 only; check T2 separately. The SKT eSIM product targets stays under 90 days, so it is a bridge only. The rule that postpaid needs a residence card comes from commercial guides only and needs review against a carrier's official document page (LG U+ need-docs did not render). Never name a carrier as a Hangyul partner without an agreement.

summary: T-money and EZL cards cost KRW 3,000–5,000 at convenience stores (GS25, CU, 7-ELEVEN) and at Seoul subway information centres. You top them up at subway machines (up to KRW 500,000) or convenience stores. They work on all public transport. WOWPASS (KRW 5,000; app or kiosks, including at airports) combines a prepaid payment card with T-money. The Climate Card can only be bought or topped up with cash or a Korean-issued card.
steps: Buy a T-money card at the airport convenience store
Top it up with cash at a subway machine or convenience store
Register the card later if you want a refund or discount features

sources.title: VISITKOREA (KTO) – Transportation Cards
sources.quote: Tmoney Card: Convenience stores nationwide (GS25, CU, 7-ELEVEN, etc.) … 3,000-5,000 won … subway ticket vending machines inside subway stations (Reload amount limited to 500,000 won max.) … Climate Card: Card purchase and charging can only be done using cash or credit / debit card issued in Korea

notes: Third-party guides say convenience-store top-ups are cash only; KTO does not say so explicitly. Tell students to carry some KRW cash on arrival.

summary: Your main options from Incheon Airport are the AREX airport railroad, airport limousine buses and taxis. The AREX all-stop train from T2 to Seoul Station takes about 66–67 minutes and costs KRW 5,350 (adult). An express train also runs to Seoul Station. Limousine buses leave from stops outside arrivals: pay at the ticket booth or with a transport card or credit card, and no reservation is needed. For students with heavy luggage or a late arrival, a direct campus transfer or university shuttle (if offered) may be easier.
steps: Check your campus's nearest AREX station or limousine route
Buy a T-money card first (it works on AREX all-stop trains and buses)
If you arrive after about 22:00, plan a taxi or a pre-booked transfer
cost: AREX all-stop T2 → Seoul Station KRW 5,350 (adult); other fares vary

summary: Some universities run free or low-cost shuttles on specific arrival days. Example: Korea University's 2026 International Summer Campus ran hourly buses (11:00–19:00) from Incheon T1 Arrival Gate F to its dormitory on check-in day only. Degree-programme pickups differ by university and intake.
steps: Check whether your university offers a pickup for your intake and date
If not, book a transfer or use AREX or a limousine bus
timing: Only on the university's announced dates

topic: Orientation, arrival report and course registration (examples)
summary: Universities hold new international student orientation (often mandatory) that covers visa rules, the residence card, NHIS, part-time work permits and academic rules. Some ask you to report your arrival. Example: KU GSIS (Spring 2026) required all international freshmen to email an Arrival Report plus proof of residence card application within 5 days of arrival. Course registration runs on the university portal in fixed windows. Example: Korea University's Fall 2026 window was 24 Aug 10:00 – 25 Aug 12:00 on sugang.korea.ac.kr.
steps: Watch for the orientation date and attend
Submit the arrival report if your university asks for one
Register for courses in the portal window
Get your student ID as your university instructs
documents: Proof of residence card application (reservation receipt or certificate of application)
timing: Before the semester starts; KU GSIS: arrival report within 5 days of arrival

sources.title: Korea University GSIS – Spring 2026 New Student Orientation (PDF)
sources.quote: ALL Spring 2026 international freshmen … MUST submit an Arrival Report and a proof of ARC … within 5 days after you arrive Korea

sources.title: Korea University – [Undergraduate] 2026 Fall Semester Course Registration
sources.quote: August 24 (Tue), 2026, 10:00 AM – August 25 (Wed), 2026, 12:00 PM … https://sugang.korea.ac.kr

notes: These are institution-specific examples. Model orientation, arrival report and course registration as university-provided dates, not global rules. Student ID issuance (including IDs with bank or debit functions) differs by university and is not verified here.

topic: Emergency numbers and foreigner help lines
summary: 112 is the police; it has a 24/7 interpretation centre for English and Chinese since March 2024. 119 is fire and ambulance. 1345 is the Immigration Contact Center: weekdays 09:00–22:00, with Korean, English and Chinese only after 18:00; from abroad dial +82-1345. 1330 is the Korea Travel Helpline (KTO), also reachable as +82-2-1330 from overseas and by chat. NHIS foreigner line: 033-811-2000.
steps: Save 112, 119, 1345 and 1330 in your phone before departure
For 1345, choose your language from the menu
